defects.title: The documented host name ' ' does not select github.com and the call fails
defects.trigger: addKeyToKnownHostsCT(' ') with ssh-keyscan installed (reproduced with HOME in a tempname folder and a fake ssh-keyscan first on PATH)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) with gitCmd set: error ">> [addKeyToKnownHostsCT]  could not be added to the known hosts file in ~/.ssh/known_hosts"; with gitCmd empty: MATLAB:structRefFromNonStruct "Dot indexing is not supported for variables of this type."; known_hosts stays empty. Lines 26-31 replace only an empty name, so ' ' is passed on: grep "^  " finds nothing and 'ssh-keyscan   >> known_hosts' runs without a host (usage message, status 1)
defects.expected: github.com is checked and added, as for no input or '' (help text: "If not provided or empty or ' ' then it checks for the host: github.com"); true is returned

defects.title: The error messages fail with a dot-indexing error when gitCmd is not set
defects.trigger: with the global gitCmd empty (no toolbox function sets it) and a fake ssh-keyscan that prints nothing for the host: addKeyToKnownHostsCT('unreachable.invalid'); likewise with an ssh-keyscan that does not print its usage message
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-15) MATLAB:structRefFromNonStruct "Dot indexing is not supported for variables of this type." at line 63 instead of the function's own message
defects.expected: the error "... unreachable.invalid could not be added to the known hosts file in ~/.ssh/known_hosts" (or "... ssh-keyscan is not installed.") without depending on gitCmd

notes:
independent review T021: finding confirmed and regraded from unrecorded to error (documented input ' ' fails); test converted to the quarantine layout (the former sandbox test is described in the Purpose for when the defect is fixed). Reproduction (in a tempname sandbox): sb = tempname; mkdir(fullfile(sb,'home')); mkdir(fullfile(sb,'bin')); write fullfile(sb,'bin','ssh-keyscan') as '#!/bin/sh
if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then echo "usage: ssh-keyscan [host]" >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "# $1:22 SSH-2.0-fake" >&2
echo "$1 ssh-ed25519 AAAAfakeKey"' and chmod +x; setenv('HOME', fullfile(sb,'home')); setenv('PATH', [fullfile(sb,'bin') pathsep getenv('PATH')]); global gitCmd gitConf; gitCmd = struct('lead','>>','success',' ok','trail','
'); gitConf = struct('printLevel',1); addKeyToKnownHostsCT(' ')  -> error '>> [addKeyToKnownHostsCT]  could not be added ...'; in the same sandbox addKeyToKnownHostsCT('') returns true and writes the github.com key. Reach: only the call form with hostName = ' ' (a blank, non-empty name) reaches the defect; no src/ function calls addKeyToKnownHostsCT at all (grep), so no src caller is blocked. Lead decision: test/verifiedTests/base/testInstall/testAddKeyToKnownHosts.m (test of addKeyToKnownHosts) still calls addKeyToKnownHostsCT() and ('github.com'), ('github123.co') and asserts on them; it does not use the ' ' form, but it now asserts behaviour of a quarantined function (not edited here: other tests may not be changed).
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's reproduction with a stand-in ssh-keyscan: hostName ' ', documented as github.com, errors)

defects.title: Copies of a solver object share one parameter map
defects.trigger: o1 = COBRArrowSolver('GLPK'); o2 = o1; o2 = o2.setParameter('k', 1); o1.parameters.keys (likewise removeParameter on a copy, or any of them on an object passed to a function)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) o1.parameters.keys is {'k'} after o2.setParameter; after o1 = o1.setParameter('m', 2); o3 = o1; o3 = o3.removeParameter('m') o1 has lost 'm'; f = @(s) s.setParameter('fromFunction', 3); f(o1) adds 'fromFunction' to o1. COBRArrowSolver is a value class, but its parameters property is a containers.Map, which is a handle (only clearParameters gives the copy a new map: o1 kept Count 2 after o4 = o1; o4 = o4.clearParameters())
defects.expected: the original keeps its parameters: a value object whose methods return the updated instance changes only the object the caller assigns the result to

notes: independent review T021: finding confirmed; regraded from limitation to wrong-result (R5: copying a value object is an allowed input, the class is a value class whose mutators return the updated instance, so the evident intent is value semantics, and the caller's original object is silently changed - also when an object is merely passed to a function that sets a parameter). Test converted to the quarantine layout. Reproduction: o1 = COBRArrowSolver('GLPK'); o2 = o1; o2 = o2.setParameter('k', 1); o1.parameters.keys  % {'k'}, expected {}. Reach: only call forms that keep two references to one instance (o2 = o1, an instance passed into a function or stored in a struct/cell) and then call setParameter or removeParameter on one of them while the other is used. The only src/ user, COBRArrow.optimizeModel (src/base/cobrarrow/COBRArrow.m, lines 441-449), creates its own default COBRArrowSolver or reads solver.name/solver.parameters (jsonencode) without calling a mutator, so it does not reach the defect. Lead decision: confirm wrong-result vs the earlier limitation grading (the class's documented example usage o = o.setParameter(...) on one variable is unaffected).
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's MATLAB reproduction: setParameter on a copy changes the original; wrong-result accepted)

defects.title: The default basePath does nothing on Windows
defects.trigger: editCobraToolboxPath([], '', 'add') (or any call that omits basePath or passes it empty) on Windows, where which('initVonBertalanffy') returns a path with backslashes; reproduced on Linux with a stand-in which in the current folder that returns the real path with every '/' replaced by '\'
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) "new folders on path after add: 0 of 6; path changed: 0", no error and no message; with the real which the same call adds 6 of 6. Line 21 strips 'vonBertalanffy/initVonBertalanffy.m' with a hard-coded '/', so basePath stays the path of the .m file and dir() lists no folder below it
defects.expected: basePath is the thermo folder on every platform (strip ['vonBertalanffy' filesep 'initVonBertalanffy.m'] or use fileparts), and the folders below it that contain the pattern are added or removed as documented

notes: independent review T021: finding confirmed (Windows-only, reproduced on Linux with a stand-in which.m in a tempname folder made the current folder: varargout{1} = strrep(builtin('which','initVonBertalanffy'), '/', '\') for that name, builtin('which', ...) otherwise); graded unusable-option (documented default basePath does nothing, silently); test converted to the quarantine layout (the former Linux test is described in the Purpose). Reproduction: cd(<tempname folder holding the stand-in which.m>); pathBefore = path; editCobraToolboxPath([], '', 'add'); isequal(path, pathBefore)  % true, expected the 6 thermo */new folders added (control with the real which adds 6 of 6). Reach: only calls that omit basePath or pass it empty, and only on Windows. src/ callers: src/analysis/thermo/trainingModel/new/driver_createTrainingModel.m passes an explicit basePath (built with the same hard-coded '/' in its own code, and the folder is not on the MATLAB path); initCobraToolbox.m (repository root, not src/) passes an explicit basePath built with filesep. No src/ function uses the default form, so none is blocked. Lead decision: whether a Windows-only default-path defect should quarantine (the Linux behaviour was fully tested before).
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's reproduction with a stand-in which() returning Windows paths: default basePath adds 0 of 6 folders; documented default on a supported platform)

defects.title: Saving fails for every output format except mol

defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) MATLAB:cellRefFromNonCell "Brace indexing is not supported for variables of this type." for all four formats (the same calls without the third argument return the converted text): newFormat is a char for these formats and line 124 writes newFormat{:}
defects.expected: the converted text is returned and written to the save location

defects.title: A scratch file named tmp is written into the current folder and left there
defects.trigger: any SMILES or InChI input, e.g. openBabelConverter('C[C@@H](C(=O)O)N', 'inchi')
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-17) after the calls the current folder holds a file 'tmp' with the input string; an existing file of that name is overwritten
defects.expected: a tempname file that is deleted after the conversion

notes: independent review T021: all three findings confirmed with a stand-in obabel (shell script in a tempname bin folder put first on PATH; usage text with status 1 without arguments, canned L-alanine output per -o format), plus the tmp-file side effect; test converted to the quarantine layout. Without saving, smiles/inchikey/inchi/mol/rinchi outputs parse correctly with that stand-in; mol output saved to a file name works. Reproduction: cd(tempname-folder); setenv('PATH', [stubBin pathsep getenv('PATH')]); openBabelConverter('InChI=1S/C3H7NO2/c1-2(4)3(5)6/h2H,4H2,1H3,(H,5,6)/t2-/m0/s1', 'smiles', fullfile(pwd,'out.smi'))  % Brace indexing error; openBabelConverter('C[C@@H](C(=O)O)N', 'mol', pwd)  % Invalid file identifier; openBabelConverter('C[C@@H](C(=O)O)N', 'rxn')  % returns []. Reach (call forms): (a) a non-empty third argument with outputFormat smiles/inchi/inchikey/rinchi; (b) a third argument naming an existing folder; (c) outputFormat 'rxn'. src/ callers: obtainMetStructures (lines 276, 365) uses 'mol' with a file name [saveFileDir metList{i} '.mol'] - does not reach (a)-(c); metaboliteStructuresTable (lines 41, 46, 51) uses 'inchikey'/'inchi'/'smiles' without a third argument - does not reach (a)-(c). Both reach only the tmp-file limitation, which does not block. So no src/ caller is blocked.
confirmed_by: lead (review T021; writer's reproductions with a stand-in obabel: saving fails for non-mol outputs, folder saveFileDir errors, 'rxn' returns [])

notes: independent review T021: finding NOT reproduced, so not a defect: in R2025a brace assignment into the empty char IDsAdded = '' converts it to a cell (probe: x = ''; x{1,1} = 'a' -> class cell), and with a stand-in obabel the function stores the key and SMILES and logs them in a 4x3 IDsAdded. The test stays TESTED and now covers the conversion lines 44-64 (previously exempt) with a stand-in obabel written by the test into a tempname folder put first on PATH (restored; prepareTest('needsUnix', true)): key and SMILES both missing (NaN), key present + SMILES empty, SMILES present + key empty, and an InChI for which the stand-in prints Open Babel's error text (nothing stored or logged). Every line covered, no exemption. Callee note (convertInchiString2format, not this function): with real Open Babel ('obabel -:"InChI=..." -i inchi -o smiles -xc' prints 'C[C@@H](C(=O)O)N<TAB>') the returned SMILES keeps a trailing tab because only newlines and '1 molecule converted' are removed; the test compares SMILES with strtrim so it does not pin that. Earlier suspicion (wave notes) still unconfirmed: contains(NaN,'Error') at lines 46/58 would error if convertInchiString2format returned NaN ('Missing or unknown output file'), which needs a broken Open Babel install.
